findings.delegated: Read torque-angle records and propose quality containment; quantity beyond 5 requires Quality Supervisor; above 50 escalates to Plant Quality Manager.
findings.discovered: Synthetic service grant exposes a work-order write operation while the approved task is recommendation only.
findings.nextEvidence: Exact MES principal grant, policy version, tool dispatch/broker receipt, authoritative MES quality-status readback.
findings.notEstablished: No independently witnessed unauthorized hold release or MES change is established by this finding.
findings.title: Torque-monitor tool path can write MES work orders beyond recommendation-only delegation

findings.delegated: Identify porosity candidates under validated model, recipe, camera and part-variant conditions; route suspect parts to a quality owner.
findings.discovered: New inspection conditions are represented in the synthetic source; defect prevalence and classifier false-accept behavior are distinct.
findings.nextEvidence: Qualified part-variant test set, lighting/recipe revision, independently labeled false-accept/false-reject samples, QMS disposition.
findings.notEstablished: A change in observed defect prevalence alone does not prove model drift or a quality escape.
findings.title: Inspection part variant and lighting change require validation evidence

findings.delegated: Generate a demand forecast and propose, but do not commit, master production schedule changes during a frozen horizon.
findings.discovered: Synthetic plan proposal changes the approved schedule by 42% against a 25% local proposal-review band.
findings.nextEvidence: Planner approval with exact schedule version, capacity/material feasibility and target APS commit record.
findings.notEstablished: A proposed plan is not an applied APS or ERP scheduling change.
findings.title: A forecast-based schedule revision crosses the frozen production-planning window

findings.delegated: Read inventory and vendor data; propose purchase orders within eligible part, approved vendor and amount limits.
findings.discovered: A synthetic $26,500 order proposal crosses a $15,000 buyer review threshold; tool surface includes a create-PO operation.
findings.nextEvidence: Approved vendor/part mapping, duplicate PO check, buyer authorization and ERP-issued purchase order receipt.
findings.notEstablished: A proposed order, post-run token overage or callable ERP endpoint is not proof of a committed purchase.
findings.title: Purchase-order proposal exceeds buyer-review amount and requires qualified approval

findings.delegated: Evaluate vibration/temperature measurements, recommend maintenance and request a CMMS case.
findings.discovered: Spindle-health agent can request a ticket, but its AI recommendation is not a machine stop or approved outage.
findings.nextEvidence: CMMS work-order lifecycle, authorized outage permit, maintenance-completion receipt and machine-state witness.
findings.notEstablished: Creating a CMMS ticket is not evidence that work was performed or that a machine restarted safely.
findings.title: Maintenance recommendation and physical equipment intervention require different authorization

findings.delegated: Recommend supplier-quality review of incoming lots; final receiving/QMS disposition belongs to authorized Supplier Quality Engineering.
findings.discovered: Synthetic supplier-part qualification is expired or unavailable for the received revision, independent of purchase-order eligibility.
findings.nextEvidence: Supplier-part-site/revision qualification, current PPAP approval, incoming inspection, NCR/MRB disposition and QMS lot readback.
findings.notEstablished: No source-qualified disposition or unauthorized receiving release has been established.
findings.title: Incoming casting lot cannot be released without valid supplier-part-site qualification

findings.delegated: Propose feasible finite-capacity sequence, while committed production schedule changes require authorized planner release.
findings.discovered: Synthetic source path exposes APS schedule.write beyond proposal-only operation; release mediation and downstream witness are unproven.
findings.nextEvidence: Approved frozen-horizon policy, exact principal, schedule gate receipt, APS/MES post-release version and capacity validation.
findings.notEstablished: No claim that an unauthorized schedule was actually released in production.
findings.title: Schedule-writing path lacks qualified mediation and application-effect evidence

findings.delegated: Read test metrics and propose permitted bounded tuning parameters during an approved test phase.
findings.discovered: Fixture code path lists 19 writable parameters while its approved test recipe delegates three.
findings.nextEvidence: Parameter/range manifest, effective controller principal, dispatch enforcement receipt and independent measured setpoint.
findings.notEstablished: A source-reachable parameter does not prove the agent issued a command or changed a controller.
findings.title: Test stand exposes nineteen writable parameters but only three are delegated

findings.delegated: Read bin inventory, propose pick tasks and replenishment; shipment of quality-held material requires QMS release and a bound WMS actor.
findings.discovered: Fixture service identity is shared and the available pick path has no established qualified lot-hold predicate.
findings.nextEvidence: Authoritative QMS hold status, exact WMS principal, WMS pick/pack/ship record and target-side shipment acknowledgment.
findings.notEstablished: An exposed picking path is not proof that held goods were shipped.
findings.title: Shared warehouse identity and missing hold check expose quality-held inventory
